🤖 Android

Authenticator Set Up

Microsoft Authenticator setup guide — all mariners

This Help is tailored for an Android phone. If you are using an iPhone, please click the following link: iPhone Setup Guide
1

Download and install Microsoft Authenticator

Figure 1
Tap to open in the Google Play Store →
2

Verify Authenticator app settings (required)

Update notification and battery settings for the Authenticator app that was just installed. Also, enable Authenticator as a passkey service. Click here: Verify Authenticator App Settings
3

Register your account with Authenticator

  • Click on this link: mysignins.microsoft.com/security-info
  • Log in using your credentials
⚠️ Important
Some mariners may not see the screens shown in fig. 2 / fig. 3 and will be taken directly to the screen shown in fig. 4.
  • Select "+ Add sign-in method" (fig. 2)
  • Select "Microsoft Authenticator" (fig. 3)
  • Select "Next" (you already installed Authenticator) (fig. 4)
Figure 2
Tap "+ Add sign-in method"
Figure 3
Select "Microsoft Authenticator"
Figure 4
Tap "Next"
  • Select "Pair your account to the app by clicking this link" (fig. 5)
  • Follow the prompts
Figure 5
Tap "Pair your account to the app by clicking this link"
4

Create a passkey for your account

⚠️ Important
The screens below are shown from an iPhone for illustration. The steps and options are the same on Android — only the visual appearance will differ slightly.
  • Open the Authenticator App
  • Select your account (fig. 6)
  • Select "Create a passkey" (fig. 7)
  • Select "Sign in" (fig. 8)
  • Sign in to your account
  • At this point, Authenticator is set up and you are logged in to Authenticator
Figure 6
Select your account
Figure 7
Select "Create a passkey"
Figure 8
Tap "Sign in" and follow the prompts
5

How to log into an app

  • Open a vessel mobile app (Confluence, Dayforce, Suti, etc.)
  • Select "Continue with Microsoft" (fig. 9)
Figure 9
Select "Continue with Microsoft"
6

Possible scenarios for what happens next

⚠️ Important
What screens you see next can vary based on the type of phone, the phone's operating system, and the app you are using.
  • You may be logged into the application immediately
  • It may use biometrics to log you in (fingerprint, etc.)
  • You may see "Use Passkey" as an option — take it
  • You may have to key in your log-in ID and password
  • You may receive the screen below and a pop-up notification to "Approve sign-in?" (fig. 10)
    • Note the two-digit number and tap the notification
    • Key in the two-digit number and tap "Yes" (fig. 11)
Figure 10
Note the two-digit number shown
Figure 11
Enter it in Authenticator and tap "Yes"
